parts.title: My noisy neighbour
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
For two months, the flat above mine was empty, and I enjoyed the silence. Then a young man moved in, and everything changed. Every evening at about eleven, I heard loud music through the ceiling, and sometimes I even heard him singing.

At first, I was too shy to complain. I put a pillow over my head and hoped that he would stop. After a week, I was so tired at work that my boss asked if I was ill. I decided that I had to do something.

One Saturday, I knocked on his door, feeling very nervous. To my surprise, he was extremely polite. He told me that he was a night-shift nurse and that he played music to relax when he came home, but he had not realised that the walls were so thin. He apologised several times and promised to use headphones.

Since then, we have become friends. Last week, he brought me a cake as a thank-you, and I invited him for dinner. It is funny to think that I nearly wrote an angry letter instead.

questions.prompt: What changed when the young man moved in?
options: There was loud music at night
questions.explanation: Every evening she heard loud music through the ceiling.

questions.prompt: Why didn't the writer complain at first?
questions.explanation: She says she was too shy to complain.

questions.prompt: What made the writer decide to act?
questions.explanation: She was so tired at work that her boss asked if she was ill.

questions.prompt: Why did the neighbour play music?
questions.explanation: He played music to relax when he came home from his night shift.

questions.prompt: How did the story end?
questions.explanation: They became friends, and he brought her a cake.

parts.title: Moving to a new neighbourhood
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
When my family moved to the town of Millbrook last year, I was very sad to leave my old friends. [1] Our new street looked quiet and a little boring, and I wondered how I would ever be happy there.

On our first Saturday, the family next door knocked on our door. [2] They brought a plate of home-made biscuits and a map of the area with their favourite places marked on it. Their daughter, Jess, was the same age as me, and she offered to show me around.

Jess took me to the park, the library and a small café. [3] By the end of the afternoon, I had met six people, and I could remember most of their names. I realised that Millbrook was not as boring as I had expected.

Now, a year later, I feel completely at home. [4] On Friday evenings, a group of us play football in the park, and in summer we all have a barbecue in Jess's garden. [5] I still miss my old friends, but I am grateful that moving brought me so many new ones.
sentences: I know almost everyone in our street now.
It is strange to think that I did not want to come here.
Jess's brother plays the guitar in a band.
They had come to welcome us to the street.
The owner smiled at Jess and introduced me to everyone in the café.
Everything in town was unfamiliar, and I did not know a single person.

gaps.explanation: "Unfamiliar" explains why the town felt boring and the street looked dull.
"They had come to welcome us" explains why the neighbours knocked and brought biscuits.
The owner introduced her to people, which leads to "met six people".
Knowing everyone in the street leads to the football and barbecue examples.
"I did not want to come" contrasts with the happy ending and the sentence "I still miss my old friends".

parts.title: A note to the neighbours
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Dear neighbours, We are having a small party next Saturday evening for our daughter's birthday. We are sorry in advance [1] the noise, so please [2] us know if it disturbs you. The party will [3] at about eleven o'clock. If you [4] like to join us, you are very welcome. We have [5] bought enough food for everyone. We look forward to [6] you there!

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: "Sorry for the noise" is the usual phrase.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: "Let us know" means to inform us.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: After "will" we use the basic form of the verb.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "If you would like to" is a polite invitation.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Already bought" shows that the food is ready before the party.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: "Look forward to" is followed by the -ing form.

parts.title: Our community garden
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Our neighbourhood needs your help! The community garden on Elm Street is [1] longer used because the gate is broken. We are asking everybody who lives [2] the area to give a little time. Last month, some neighbours [3] painted the fence, and it looks lovely. If you [4] free on Saturday morning, please come and join us. You do not have to be good [5] gardening: we will show you what to do. Tea and cake [6] be provided for all the helpers.

gaps.explanation: "Have painted" is the present perfect, referring to last month's work.
"If you are free" is a condition about being available.
"Will be provided" is a promise about the future.

parts.title: Welcome to the community centre
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: gillian
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome to the Oakfield Community Centre. We are open from nine in the morning until ten at night, six days a week. We are closed on Mondays. There is a café on the ground floor, where a cup of tea costs one pound. On Tuesday afternoons, there is a free yoga class for beginners. On Wednesdays, children can join the art club, which meets at four o'clock. The big hall can be hired for parties, and it costs forty pounds for the evening. If you would like to be a volunteer, please speak to Mrs Dunn at reception. We also have a noticeboard where you can advertise things that you want to sell. Thank you for coming.

gaps.explanation: The centre is closed on Mondays.

gaps.explanation: A cup of tea costs one pound.

gaps.prompt: There is a free ___ class on Tuesdays
gaps.explanation: There is a free yoga class for beginners on Tuesday afternoons.

gaps.prompt: The art club meets at ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: The art club meets at four o'clock.

parts.title: A community worker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: Today I'm talking to Donna Rahman, a community worker. Donna, why did you choose this job?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: I grew up in a block of flats where everybody knew each other. When I moved to the city, I missed that feeling, and I decided to help other people find it.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What do you organise?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: Lots of things: street parties, a weekly lunch for older people and repair days, when neighbours bring broken bikes and toys, and volunteers fix them for free.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What is the biggest problem in your area?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: Loneliness. Many people live next to each other for years and never speak. Often, the only thing needed is somebody to say hello first.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What has worked best?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: A wall of messages outside the library. People pin up notes, like offers to help with shopping or requests for a guitar teacher. It has brought many people together.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: Any funny memories?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: At our last street party, a man arrived with a goat. He said it was part of his family and could not be left at home.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What are your plans?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: I'm going to open a tool library, where people can borrow drills, ladders and lawnmowers instead of buying them.

questions.prompt: Why did Donna want to become a community worker?
questions.explanation: She grew up where everybody knew each other and missed that feeling.

questions.prompt: What does she organise?
questions.explanation: She organises street parties, weekly lunches and repair days.

questions.prompt: What does she think is the biggest problem?
questions.explanation: She says the biggest problem is loneliness.

questions.prompt: What has worked best?
questions.explanation: A wall of messages outside the library has brought many people together.

questions.prompt: What happened at the last street party?
questions.explanation: A man arrived with a goat.

questions.prompt: What will she open?
questions.explanation: She will open a tool library.
